source_verification_receipts.version: JRSSB 88(3), published 12 January 2026; author camera-ready corroboration at arXiv:2112.13495v4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published article studies SMRDs under local interference, gives finite-sample properties and CLTs; Theorem 4.7 gives consistency of a conservative variance estimator under its stated sequence conditions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; p. 23, “Further Questions on MRDs” rank-one example
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives minimum-asymptotic-variance linearly adjusted MRD estimators and explicitly notes non-normal limits through a rank-one doubly randomized sum.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; pp. 1--2; p. 5 equation (2) and Assumption 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses a maximum of one-way and usual standard errors, is exact in Gaussian regimes and conservative otherwise, and works under dissociated separately exchangeable arrays rather than a fixed-schedule randomization experiment.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1504.01689, accessible author version; cited TOCT primary is access-restricted
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines swap-based slice influences and proves a low-degree harmonic single-slice invariance principle; it does not itself state the proposed two-slice rectangular MRD result.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2305.09906, preprint corresponding to the cited Journal of Econometrics article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper computes exact binary-outcome randomized-experiment intervals by permutation-test inversion, with O(n log n) tests for balanced designs.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the completion-game handle with a formal finite input specification: a fixed quantizer, orbit equivalence relation, finite completion coordinates and constraints, explicit restriction/lifting kernels, and chi as a displayed maximum over that declared finite table; otherwise relabel the current certificate as an OEQ.

Repair the frontier OEQ by requiring limsup_n sup_Y E_Y[length(I_n)]/M(Y) <= R_alpha(rho)+epsilon, and state whether the certificate yields this for all sufficiently large n or only along a subsequence.

Retag aggregate-low-influence as a proposal-specific sufficient condition, justify its marketplace plausibility, and present the product-slice influence algebra as the derivation that connects it to Filmus et al.'s actual single-slice condition.

recommended_next_step: Revise the finite completion-game object into a mathematically specified finite experiment and correct the OEQ's asymptotic attainment quantifier; the all-policy MRD frontier remains a field-tier novel kernel after those repairs.
